description: Hardware Hacking Village focuses on embedded hardware exploration, printed circuit board assembly, soldering fundamentals, and physical microcontroller security. Talks cover soldering workshop kits, HackerBox component builds, foundational hardware hacking techniques, and keystroke injection hardware.

talks.title: Learn to Solder the Badge Buddy Kit
talks.teaser: Guides viewers through essential soldering skills and through-hole component assembly using the Badge Buddy kit.
talks.summary:
In this beginner-friendly workshop from the DEF CON Safe Mode Hardware Hacking Village, Joe from HackerBoxes teaches the fundamentals of through-hole electronics soldering. Opening at 00:00, Joe introduces the "Badge Buddy" soldering kit, an interactive printed circuit board featuring flashing LEDs designed to teach soldering skills.

At 09:00, he explains essential soldering equipment—including temperature-controlled soldering irons, rosin-core solder, flux pens, and isopropyl alcohol cleaning solvents to remove sticky flux residue.

At 18:01 and 27:00, Joe demonstrates proper iron positioning, pad heating, applying solder to create clean concave fillets, and safely trimming component leads. Concluding at 36:00, he demonstrates desoldering techniques using copper solder wick to fix accidental solder bridges, encouraging newcomers to gain confidence in hardware fabrication. talks.title: HackerBox 0057 Build
talks.teaser: Walks through unboxing, assembling, and programming the HackerBox 0057 hardware electronics project.
talks.summary:
Maker and hardware designer Joseph Long presents a hands-on assembly workshop for HackerBox 0057 in the Hardware Hacking Village, providing a build walkthrough for an interactive handheld cybersecurity multitool [00:00, 00:06].

Long guides builders through through-hole and surface-mount soldering techniques, detailing component placement for LiPo battery charging modules, tactile switches, an edge-firing infrared transceiver, and an integrated five-way navigation joystick [07:08, 15:43, 26:01]. He demonstrates firmware programming on the onboard microcontroller, walking through hardware diagnostic routines and showcasing multi-protocol capabilities including Wi-Fi scanning, Bluetooth LE control, and IR signal replication [35:08].

talks.title: Hardware Hacking 101
talks.teaser: Provides an introductory primer on hardware reverse engineering, circuit analysis, and common physical attack vectors.
talks.summary:
Hardware Hacking and Physical Security

This talk covers hardware hacking techniques and physical security analysis. Topics include circuit board analysis, side-channel attacks, firmware extraction, and low-level debugging of hardware systems.
